how many neutrons does hydrogen have | number of neutrons in hydrogen | hydrogen neutrons => Most hydrogen atoms have 0 neutrons, just one proton and one electron. Rare forms called deuterium and tritium have 1 and 2 neutrons.
who discovered hydrogen | when was hydrogen discovered | who found hydrogen | hydrogen discovery => Henry Cavendish identified hydrogen as an element in 1766. Antoine Lavoisier gave it its name in 1783.
where does the name hydrogen come from | why is hydrogen called hydrogen | what does hydrogen mean | how did hydrogen get its name => Hydrogen comes from Greek words meaning 'water maker', because it makes water when it burns.
what is hydrogen used for | hydrogen uses | what do we use hydrogen for | why is hydrogen useful => Hydrogen is used to make ammonia for fertilizer, to process fuels, and as rocket fuel. It can also power fuel cell cars.

how many electron shells does hydrogen have | hydrogen bohr model | electron arrangement of hydrogen | how are the electrons arranged in hydrogen => Hydrogen has 1 electron shell, holding 1 electron.
what is the electron configuration of hydrogen | hydrogen electron configuration | hydrogen electron config => The electron configuration of Hydrogen is 1s1.
how many valence electrons does hydrogen have | hydrogen valence electrons | outer electrons in hydrogen => Hydrogen has 1 valence electron, the electron in its outer shell.
is hydrogen radioactive | does hydrogen have radiation | does hydrogen give off radiation => Normal hydrogen is not radioactive. A rare form called tritium is radioactive and is used in glowing watch dials and exit signs.

how many valence electrons does bromine have | bromine valence electrons | outer electrons in bromine => Bromine has 7 valence electrons, the electrons in its outer shell. It wants one more to fill its shell, so it reacts easily.
is bromine radioactive | does bromine have radiation | does bromine give off radiation => No, bromine is not radioactive in its normal form. It has at least one stable isotope.
what is the atomic mass of krypton | krypton atomic mass | atomic weight of krypton | how heavy is a krypton atom | whats the mass of krypton on the periodic table => The atomic mass of krypton is about 83.798 u (atomic mass units). That's the average mass of its atoms as found in nature.
what group is krypton in | what period is krypton in | where is krypton on the periodic table | krypton group and period => Krypton is in group 18 and period 4 of the periodic table, in the p-block.
is krypton a metal | what type of element is krypton | is krypton a metal or nonmetal | what family is krypton in | krypton element category => No, krypton is a nonmetal. It's a noble gas, so it hardly reacts with anything.
how many protons does krypton have | how many electrons does krypton have | krypton protons and electrons | number of protons in krypton => Krypton has 36 protons in its nucleus. A neutral krypton atom also has 36 electrons.
how many neutrons does krypton have | number of neutrons in krypton | krypton neutrons => Most krypton atoms are krypton-84 (about 57% of it in nature), which has 48 neutrons. Other isotopes of krypton have different numbers of neutrons.
who discovered krypton | when was krypton discovered | who found krypton | krypton discovery => William Ramsay and Morris Travers discovered krypton in 1898.
where does the name krypton come from | why is krypton called krypton | what does krypton mean | how did krypton get its name => Krypton comes from kryptos, the Greek word for hidden.
what is krypton used for | krypton uses | what do we use krypton for | why is krypton useful => Krypton is used in some flash lamps for photography, high efficiency windows and certain lights.
what is the melting point of krypton | at what temperature does krypton melt | how hot does krypton have to be to melt | krypton melting point => Krypton melts at about -157 °C (-251 °F). It's a gas at room temperature.
what is the boiling point of krypton | at what temperature does krypton boil | when does krypton turn into a gas | krypton boiling point => Krypton boils at about -153 °C (-244 °F). That's why it's a gas at room temperature.
how many electron shells does krypton have | krypton bohr model | electron arrangement of krypton | how are the electrons arranged in krypton => Krypton has 4 electron shells. The electrons are arranged 2, 8, 18, 8, from the inside out.
what is the electron configuration of krypton | krypton electron configuration | krypton electron config => The electron configuration of Krypton is [Ar] 3d10 4s2 4p6.
how many valence electrons does krypton have | krypton valence electrons | outer electrons in krypton => Krypton has 8 valence electrons, the electrons in its outer shell. Its outer shell is full, which is why it hardly reacts.
is krypton radioactive | does krypton have radiation | does krypton give off radiation => No, krypton is not radioactive in its normal form. It has at least one stable isotope.

what group is palladium in | what period is palladium in | where is palladium on the periodic table | palladium group and period => Palladium is in group 10 and period 5 of the periodic table, in the d-block.
is palladium a metal | what type of element is palladium | is palladium a metal or nonmetal | what family is palladium in | palladium element category => Yes, palladium is a metal. It's a transition metal.
how many protons does palladium have | how many electrons does palladium have | palladium protons and electrons | number of protons in palladium => Palladium has 46 protons in its nucleus. A neutral palladium atom also has 46 electrons.
how many neutrons does palladium have | number of neutrons in palladium | palladium neutrons => Most palladium atoms are palladium-106 (the most common form, about 27% of it in nature), which has 60 neutrons. Other isotopes of palladium have different numbers of neutrons.
who discovered palladium | when was palladium discovered | who found palladium | palladium discovery => William Hyde Wollaston discovered palladium in 1803.
where does the name palladium come from | why is palladium called palladium | what does palladium mean | how did palladium get its name => Palladium is named after the asteroid Pallas, which had just been discovered.
what is palladium used for | palladium uses | what do we use palladium for | why is palladium useful => Palladium is used in catalytic converters in cars, in electronics, dentistry and jewelry.

what is the density of palladium | how dense is palladium | is palladium heavy for its size | palladium density => Palladium has a density of about 12 g/cm³. That's about 12 times as dense as water.
how many electron shells does palladium have | palladium bohr model | electron arrangement of palladium | how are the electrons arranged in palladium => Palladium has 4 electron shells. The electrons are arranged 2, 8, 18, 18, from the inside out.
what is the electron configuration of palladium | palladium electron configuration | palladium electron config => The electron configuration of Palladium is [Kr] 4d10.
is palladium radioactive | does palladium have radiation | does palladium give off radiation => No, palladium is not radioactive in its normal form. It has at least one stable isotope.

what is the atomic mass of lanthanum | lanthanum atomic mass | atomic weight of lanthanum | how heavy is a lanthanum atom | whats the mass of lanthanum on the periodic table => The atomic mass of lanthanum is about 138.905 u (atomic mass units). That's the average mass of its atoms as found in nature.
what group is lanthanum in | what period is lanthanum in | where is lanthanum on the periodic table | lanthanum group and period => Lanthanum is in period 6, in the lanthanide series. That's the first of the two separate rows usually drawn below the main periodic table.
is lanthanum a metal | what type of element is lanthanum | is lanthanum a metal or nonmetal | what family is lanthanum in | lanthanum element category => Yes, lanthanum is a metal. It's a lanthanide, one of the rare earth metals.
how many protons does lanthanum have | how many electrons does lanthanum have | lanthanum protons and electrons | number of protons in lanthanum => Lanthanum has 57 protons in its nucleus. A neutral lanthanum atom also has 57 electrons.
how many neutrons does lanthanum have | number of neutrons in lanthanum | lanthanum neutrons => Most lanthanum atoms are lanthanum-139 (almost all of it in nature), which has 82 neutrons. Other isotopes of lanthanum have different numbers of neutrons.
who discovered lanthanum | when was lanthanum discovered | who found lanthanum | lanthanum discovery => Carl Gustaf Mosander discovered lanthanum in 1839.
where does the name lanthanum come from | why is lanthanum called lanthanum | what does lanthanum mean | how did lanthanum get its name => Lanthanum comes from lanthanein, Greek for to lie hidden, because it hid in another mineral.
what is lanthanum used for | lanthanum uses | what do we use lanthanum for | why is lanthanum useful => Lanthanum is used in camera lenses and in batteries for hybrid cars.
what is the melting point of lanthanum | at what temperature does lanthanum melt | how hot does lanthanum have to be to melt | lanthanum melting point => Lanthanum melts at about 920 °C (1,688 °F).
what is the boiling point of lanthanum | at what temperature does lanthanum boil | when does lanthanum turn into a gas | lanthanum boiling point => Lanthanum boils at about 3,464 °C (6,267 °F).
what is the density of lanthanum | how dense is lanthanum | is lanthanum heavy for its size | lanthanum density => Lanthanum has a density of about 6.15 g/cm³. That's about 6.2 times as dense as water.
how many electron shells does lanthanum have | lanthanum bohr model | electron arrangement of lanthanum | how are the electrons arranged in lanthanum => Lanthanum has 6 electron shells. The electrons are arranged 2, 8, 18, 18, 9, 2, from the inside out.
what is the electron configuration of lanthanum | lanthanum electron configuration | lanthanum electron config => The electron configuration of Lanthanum is [Xe] 5d1 6s2.

what group is holmium in | what period is holmium in | where is holmium on the periodic table | holmium group and period => Holmium is in period 6, in the lanthanide series. That's the first of the two separate rows usually drawn below the main periodic table.
is holmium a metal | what type of element is holmium | is holmium a metal or nonmetal | what family is holmium in | holmium element category => Yes, holmium is a metal. It's a lanthanide, one of the rare earth metals.
how many protons does holmium have | how many electrons does holmium have | holmium protons and electrons | number of protons in holmium => Holmium has 67 protons in its nucleus. A neutral holmium atom also has 67 electrons.
how many neutrons does holmium have | number of neutrons in holmium | holmium neutrons => Most holmium atoms are holmium-165 (almost all of it in nature), which has 98 neutrons. Other isotopes of holmium have different numbers of neutrons.
who discovered holmium | when was holmium discovered | who found holmium | holmium discovery => Per Teodor Cleve discovered holmium in 1878. Marc Delafontaine and Jacques Louis Soret spotted it the same year.
where does the name holmium come from | why is holmium called holmium | what does holmium mean | how did holmium get its name => Holmium comes from Holmia, the Latin name for Stockholm.
what is holmium used for | holmium uses | what do we use holmium for | why is holmium useful => Holmium is used in medical lasers and in very strong magnets.
what is the melting point of holmium | at what temperature does holmium melt | how hot does holmium have to be to melt | holmium melting point => Holmium melts at about 1,461 °C (2,662 °F).
what is the boiling point of holmium | at what temperature does holmium boil | when does holmium turn into a gas | holmium boiling point => Holmium boils at about 2,600 °C (4,712 °F).
what is the density of holmium | how dense is holmium | is holmium heavy for its size | holmium density => Holmium has a density of about 8.8 g/cm³. That's about 8.8 times as dense as water.
how many electron shells does holmium have | holmium bohr model | electron arrangement of holmium | how are the electrons arranged in holmium => Holmium has 6 electron shells. The electrons are arranged 2, 8, 18, 29, 8, 2, from the inside out.
what is the electron configuration of holmium | holmium electron configuration | holmium electron config => The electron configuration of Holmium is [Xe] 4f11 6s2.
